evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The manager_restarted check at lines 1104-1116 only requires both manager PIDs to be positive, the PIDs to differ, and both invocation IDs to be nonempty and different. A guest reboot can change those same manager identity fields, so a reboot between the manager before/after captures can satisfy manager_restarted without an actual manager restart. The separate boot_id_changed check for the later reboot does not prevent this. The smallest compatible repair is to require the manager before/after boot IDs to be present and equal, in addition to the existing identity checks.
